A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphIDS study. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched despite the bibliography expansion and resulting pagination shift.

before.justification: v3 reports original intrusion-detection experiments, including benchmark performance in Table 3, computational measurements, and ablations and detection analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains the original benchmark experiments and computational measurements and reports revised attack-type diagnostics and neighborhood-depth ablation results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same E-GraphSAGE encoder, Transformer autoencoder, attention masking, joint reconstruction loss, and anomaly-scoring procedure. The default remains one hop; revised multi-hop results do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate NF-UNSW-NB15-v2/v3 and NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018-v2/v3 with the same attack categories. No dataset, task, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains CBLOF, SAFE, Anomal-E, T-MAE, and SimpleAE. The extended comparisons in Tables 5–8 retain the same CBLOF, HBOS, Isolation Forest, and PCA methods on embeddings and raw features.

E3.justification: The documented splits, preprocessing, training settings, evaluation metrics, and validation-based threshold selection are unchanged. C.5 still compares one, two, and three hops. Different thresholds in Figures 5–8 are reported outputs without a stated change to the selection procedure.

E4.justification: The existing neighborhood-depth ablation in C.5 and attack-type error analyses in Figures 5–8 receive revised evidence. Their diagnostic questions and tested configurations remain unchanged, as do the t-SNE analyses and other ablations.

E5.justification: Seed disclosures, mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, and representative density plots without error bars are unchanged. Updated standard deviations and removal of C.5's previous nonsignificance finding concern results rather than a revised statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Table 13 substantially revises multi-hop results and reverses rankings. Three-hop PR-AUC on NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018-v2 changes from 0.7482 ± 0.3526 to 0.9308 ± 0.0094, exceeding the unchanged one-hop 0.9201; on its v3 counterpart, three-hop PR-AUC changes from 0.8969 to 0.8683, falling below one-hop 0.8819. Figures 7–8 change representative Infiltration detection rates from 0.04/0.01 to 0.25/0.18, while Figure 8 Bot detection falls from 0.90 to 0.72. Plotted thresholds also change, and C.5 revises memory overhead from 24% to 29%. Main benchmark results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The reconstruction-score and MSE definitions in Equations 1–2 and positional-encoding formula in Equation 3 are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same architectural novelty, generalization, efficiency, and performance claims, including up to 99.98% PR-AUC and 99.61% macro F1.

C2.justification: C.5 replaces the tentative explanation that distant neighbors introduce noise and dilute local information with an assertion that multi-hop aggregation works without severe over-smoothing. It emphasizes dataset-dependent benefits and added latency while retaining the one-hop recommendation. Other interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: C.5 removes the explicit disclosure that the implementation supports arbitrary n-hop configurations. This does not establish removal of that capability. Software, hardware, code/model access information, and Table 14 hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 27 works remain cited, and the related-work narrative and research positioning are unchanged. References including BERT, MAE, GraphMAE, GraphSAGE, and Deep Graph Infomax receive publication metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: C.5 is locally rewritten and reparagraphed, several bibliography entries are expanded or corrected, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The main text and overall section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 5–8 are replotted with changed histogram shapes, axis ranges and ticks, and threshold annotations. Figure and table membership and numbering are retained. Bibliography expansion and the C.5 rewrite cause limited page and table reflow.

improvement.justification: v5 improves bibliographic completeness and updates C.5's discussion to reflect revised rankings. However, the PDFs do not explain the substantial replacements in Table 13 and Figures 5–8 or establish that they provide more reliable evidence. The new assertion about avoiding severe over-smoothing also lacks a corresponding diagnostic analysis. With the primary method and benchmark evidence unchanged, the net effect on paper quality cannot be reliably determined.
